title: Do Vision SAE Features Survive Image Corruptions? A Robustness Variation

original_idea.body:
# Do Vision SAE Features Survive Image Corruptions? A Robustness Variation

**Problem:** Whether interpreted vision-SAE features remain stable under standard image corruptions is unexplored.

**Direction:** Take labeled features from Prisma's pretrained vision SAEs. Apply graded corruptions to maximally-activating images and measure how feature activation decays. Rank features by corruption robustness.

**Why it matters:** Multimodal safety monitoring will rely on vision features; if brittle to mild corruption, monitors are evadable.

**Relevant context:** ViT-Prisma; ImageNet-C-style corruptions; open problem: extend MI to vision.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: brittle vision SAE features make multimodal monitors evadable, but the link to catastrophic risk is somewhat indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Apply ImageNet-C corruptions + measure activation decay over released SAEs; beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped corruption-robustness ranking of vision features, clear metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open multimodal interp audit labs deprioritize; public SAEs.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference over released vision SAEs; low compute.

novelty.reasoning: Corruption-robustness of vision SAE features appears unexplored.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Corruption-robustness of vision SAE features appears unexplored.
